text: For real-valued functions f_n and f on a common domain D, uniform convergence means: for every epsilon>0 there exists an integer N>=1 such that |f_n(x)-f(x)|<epsilon for every n>=N and every x in D. N may depend on epsilon, but not on x.
provenance: Original mathematical exposition, checked against Jiri Lebl, Basic Analysis, Definition 6.1.6: https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_puconv.html. Source consulted directly; no source prose reproduced or dataset imported.

text: For real-valued functions f_n,f on D, pointwise convergence means that for every x in D and epsilon>0 there exists an integer N>=1 such that |f_n(x)-f(x)|<epsilon for every n>=N. N may depend on x: for f_n(x)=x/n on R and f=0, an integer N>|x|/epsilon suffices.
provenance: Original mathematical exposition and independently checked example, checked against Jiri Lebl, Basic Analysis, Proposition 6.1.5: https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_puconv.html. Source consulted directly; no source prose reproduced or dataset imported.

text: Every nonempty set A of real numbers that is bounded above has a finite supremum s. It satisfies a<=s for every a in A, and for each epsilon>0 some a in A satisfies s-epsilon<a. For A=(0,1), s=1, although A has no maximum. The empty set and unbounded-above sets have no finite real supremum.
provenance: Original mathematical exposition and interval example, checked against Jiri Lebl, Basic Analysis, Definitions 1.1.2-1.1.3: https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_basicpropsrn.html; epsilon characterization checked against https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_setofreals.html. Sources consulted directly; no source prose reproduced or dataset imported.

text: For n>=1, f_n(x)=sqrt(x^2+1/n) converges uniformly to |x| on [-1,1]. Squaring gives 0<=f_n(x)-|x|<=1/sqrt(n). The maximum error equals 1/sqrt(n), attained at x=0. An integer N>epsilon^(-2) ensures error<epsilon for every n>=N and every x in [-1,1].
provenance: Original mathematical exposition of the retained example; the inequality and exact maximum were checked algebraically. Uniform-convergence definition checked against Jiri Lebl, Basic Analysis: https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_puconv.html. Source consulted directly; no source prose reproduced or dataset imported.

text: On [0,1], f_n(x)=x^n has pointwise limit f(x)=0 for x<1 and f(1)=1. Convergence is not uniform: x_n=2^(-1/n) lies below 1, yet |f_n(x_n)-f(x_n)|=1/2 for every n>=1. Thus epsilon=1/2 defeats every candidate tail index N.
provenance: Original mathematical exposition and explicit moving-point witness; the witness was checked by exponentiation. Pointwise power limits and failure of uniform convergence checked against Jiri Lebl, Basic Analysis, Section 6.1: https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_puconv.html. Source consulted directly; no source prose reproduced or dataset imported.

text: The real sequence a_n=(-1)^n is bounded by |a_n|=1 but does not converge. Its even subsequence is constantly 1 and its odd subsequence is constantly -1; a convergent sequence would give both subsequences the same limit. Boundedness alone guarantees only a convergent subsequence, by Bolzano-Weierstrass.
provenance: Original mathematical exposition, checked against Jiri Lebl, Basic Analysis, subsequences in Section 2.1: https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_seqsandlims.html; Bolzano-Weierstrass in Section 2.3: https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_bw.html. Sources consulted directly; no source prose reproduced or dataset imported.

text: A real sequence a_n converges exactly when it is Cauchy: for every epsilon>0 some integer N>=1 makes |a_m-a_n|<epsilon for all m,n>=N. Small adjacent differences are insufficient. For harmonic partial sums H_n=sum_{k=1}^n 1/k, H_{n+1}-H_n=1/(n+1) tends to 0, but H_{2n}-H_n>=n/(2n)=1/2 for every n>=1.
provenance: Original mathematical exposition and independently checked harmonic-block inequality. Cauchy quantifiers and completeness of R checked against Jiri Lebl, Basic Analysis, Definition 2.4.1 and Theorem 2.4.5: https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_cauchy.html. Source consulted directly; no source prose reproduced or dataset imported.

text: If a real sequence a_n is nondecreasing and bounded above, then a_n converges to s=sup{a_n:n>=1}. For every epsilon>0, the supremum property gives a_k>s-epsilon; monotonicity then gives s-epsilon<a_n<=s for all n>=k. For a_n=1-1/n, the supremum and limit are both 1, which no term attains.
provenance: Original mathematical exposition and independently checked example, checked against Jiri Lebl, Basic Analysis, Theorem 2.1.10 and its proof: https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_seqsandlims.html. Source consulted directly; no source prose reproduced or dataset imported.

text: For a bounded real sequence a_n, let U_N=sup{a_n:n>=N} and L_N=inf{a_n:n>=N}. The decreasing U_N converges to limsup a_n; the increasing L_N converges to liminf a_n. The sequence converges precisely when these limits agree. For a_n=(-1)^n+1/n, even terms approach 1 and odd terms approach -1, so limsup=1 and liminf=-1.
provenance: Original mathematical exposition and independently checked perturbed oscillating example, checked against Jiri Lebl, Basic Analysis, Definition 2.3.1 and Propositions 2.3.2 and 2.3.5: https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_bw.html. Source consulted directly; no source prose reproduced or dataset imported.

text: If continuous real-valued functions f_n on D, a subset of R, converge uniformly to f, then f is continuous on D. At x_0 in D, choose one index k with |f_k-f|<epsilon/3 throughout D, then choose delta>0 so |f_k(x)-f_k(x_0)|<epsilon/3 whenever x is in D and |x-x_0|<delta. The triangle inequality gives |f(x)-f(x_0)|<epsilon. Compactness of D is unnecessary.
provenance: Original mathematical exposition, checked against Jiri Lebl, Basic Analysis, Theorem 6.2.2 and its proof: https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_liminter.html. The three-error triangle bound was also checked directly. Source consulted directly; no source prose reproduced or dataset imported.
